finding.claim: GET /mirror fetches an attacker-supplied URL whose hostname is checked only with a bare suffix match, so attacker-registrable domains such as attackerexample.com pass the check and can point at internal addresses (cloud metadata, loopback, RFC 1918).
finding.source: mirror.py:11 — url query parameter of GET /mirror
finding.sink: mirror.py:16 — httpx.AsyncClient().get(url) with the unmodified attacker string

trace.note: url: str taken directly from the query string
host.endswith("example.com") — no dot boundary, so evilexample.com / attackerexample.com / foo-example.com pass; ALLOWED_SUFFIX (line 7) is unused
original url passed to httpx; DNS resolved at fetch time; no resolved-IP check
only len(r.text) returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Hostname suffix check (present, insufficient: no dot boundary, name-only, no resolved-IP check). Scheme not validated but httpx only supports http/https here. No private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, so DNS rebinding is also possible. httpx AsyncClient does not follow redirects by default, so no redirect bypass. GET only, no caller-controlled headers or body. Response body not returned (length oracle only). /ping at lines 20-24 has a hardcoded URL and is not a finding. A possible urlparse-vs-httpx parser differential was not verified (probe execution was denied) and is not reported.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is mirror.py:13, `host.endswith("example.com")`, which has no dot boundary, so attackerexample.com passes. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (mirror.py:7) is unused, and nothing blocks private, loopback, or link-local IPs before the request at mirror.py:16.
verdict.reason: The url query parameter (mirror.py:11) is attacker-controlled and unauthenticated; the suffix check at mirror.py:13 is bypassable by any attacker-registrable domain ending in "example.com", and the unmodified url is fetched at mirror.py:16 with no resolved-IP check, so an attacker-owned DNS name pointing at 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1 reaches internal addresses. The response is limited to a length oracle (mirror.py:17), which reduces impact but does not remove the SSRF.
